I'll use "Nonautomatic weighing instrument"? The text says "Non automatic electromechanical weighing instrument". I'll use that as category.
- type_designations: ["eS..."] — type eS... (prefix eS with variants)
- module_designation: The technical data mentions "when using analog load cells" and "when using digital load cells" — these are configuration variants of the instrument (load cell modules). The module designation for R76 instruments could be null. Actually the certified type includes both analog and digital load cell configurations. I'd set module_designation: null or "Not applicable". Hmm. The certified type is the weighing instrument; load cells are components. I'll leave module_designation null. Actually maybe better: null.

Description: "Non automatic electromechanical weighing instrument, Type: eS..."

Model family: Type "eS..." suggests a family. But we don't have per-model variants named. The technical data tables vary by accuracy class and load cell type (analog vs digital). These are configuration axes, not models. So model_family: omit (only include if cert covers >1 model variant). Type designation is "eS..." with ellipsis indicating a series, but no specific models listed. I'll omit model_family.

Components: The cert mentions analog load cells and digital load cells as used modules. Are these "sub-assemblies named"? The cert doesn't name specific load cell types. So components[] may not be needed. But the two tables are "Technical data when using analog load cells" vs "digital load cells" — a configuration axis: load_cell_type: analog | digital. I could use config_level for that. Characteristics:

type_level: none really — everything varies by class and configuration.

config_level: 
- axis 1: accuracy_class: (III) or (IIII)
- axis 2: load_cell_type: analog or digital

Actually the structure is a matrix: for analog load cells: class III → n ≤ 10000 (footnote 1), class IIII → n ≤ 1000 (footnote 1); n ≤ 3000 (III, footnote 2), n ≤ 1000 (IIII, footnote 2); Max: 1 kg ... 120 t (both classes); tare: ≤100% Max.

For digital: only class III; Max 1 kg ... 6000 kg; n ≤ 7500 (fn 1); n ≤ 3000 (fn 2); tare ≤100% Max.

How to encode? Use config_level entries with attribute, axis, values[{condition, value, unit_symbol, footnote_markers}].

Config axes:
1. attribute: number_of_verification_scale_intervals (single/multiple range), axis: accuracy_class & load_cell_type... Hmm, config_level takes a single axis. There are two axes: load_cell_module_type (analog/digital) and accuracy_class. I could create entries with axis combining both, e.g. axis: "load_cell_type / accuracy_class", or create separate entries per axis.

Maybe simplest: config_level entries:
- attribute: "max_capacity", axis: "load_cell_type", values: [{condition: "analog load cells, accuracy classes (III) and (IIII)", value: {min:1,max:120}, unit_symbol mixed...}] — hmm, "1 kg ... 120 t" is a range with mixed units. Value {min:1, max:120}, unit... kg to t. Could record as value string? Rule says numbers. I could record min 1 kg and max 120 t... The unit differs. Options: keep as value "1 kg ... 120 t" string? The rule says structured values strict, but mixed units is awkward. I could record value: {min: 1, max: 120} with unit_symbol null and note in description? Hmm.

Alternative: two separate conditions: value {min: 1, max: 120}, unit_symbol: null, with maybe a note. Or normalize: min 1 kg, max 120000 kg. I think safer: value: {min: 1, max: 120}, unit_symbol: null, and add description in... Actually there's no per-entry description field. Hmm.

Alternatively, emit two config-level entries: maximum_capacity_min: {condition: analog, value: 1, unit: kg} and maximum_capacity_max: {condition: analog, value: 120, unit: t}. That's cleaner. Similarly digital: min 1 kg, max 6000 kg.

Let me design config_level:

- attribute: "maximum_capacity_min", axis: "load_cell_type", values: [{condition: "analog", value: 1, unit_symbol: "kg"}, {condition: "digital", value: 1, unit_symbol: "kg"}]

- attribute: "number_of_verification_scale_intervals_multi_interval" (footnote 2), axis similar: [{condition: "(III), analog", max 3000, fn 2}, {condition: "(IIII), analog", max 1000, fn 2}, {condition: "(III), digital", max 3000, fn 2}]
- attribute: "tare_balancing_range_subtractive", axis: "load_cell_type", values: [{condition: "analog", value: {min:null,max:100}, unit_symbol: "%"}, {condition: "digital", value: {min:null,max:100}, unit_symbol: "%"}] — but "≤100 % • Max" references Max. Could include reference: value string "100 % of Max"? Rule 3: "150% of Emax" → value 150, unit "%" and separate reference characteristic. Here I can add attribute "tare_balancing_range_reference": {value: "Max"} at type level? Both configs. Maybe type_level: tare_balancing_range_reference: {value: "Max"}. Or keep simple.

Actually maybe simpler to use axis "configuration" with conditions like "analog load cells, accuracy class (III)". Let me combine axis name as "load_cell_type / accuracy_class".

Also accuracy_classes in recommendation: ["III", "IIII"] — but digital only III. Recommendation entry: id "R76-1", edition 2006, accuracy_classes ["(III)","(IIII)"] → canonical "III", "IIII". Use ["III", "IIII"].

Scheme: older certs like this are scheme A. Include scheme: "A".
